**Hyundai Motor India Limited (HMIL)** is the Indian subsidiary of the South Korean automobile manufacturer [Hyundai Motor Company](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hyundai_Motor_Company "Hyundai Motor Company"). It is the second largest car manufacturer in India by sales until 2025.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hyundai_Motor_India#cite_note-4)
## History
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Hyundai_Motor_India&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]
[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/02/HyundaiChennai.JPG/250px-HyundaiChennai.JPG?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:HyundaiChennai.JPG)Hyundai's manufacturing plant near [Chennai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chennai "Chennai"). [![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/23/Hyundai_Cars_at_the_port.jpg/250px-Hyundai_Cars_at_the_port.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Hyundai_Cars_at_the_port.jpg)Hyundai Cars at a port.
In the early 1990s, the [Indian automobile market](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Automotive_industry_in_India "Automotive industry in India") had only five major automobile manufacturers: [Maruti Suzuki](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maruti_Suzuki "Maruti Suzuki"), [Tata](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/TATA_Motors "TATA Motors") and [Mahindra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mahindra_&_Mahindra_Limited "Mahindra & Mahindra Limited"), [Hindustan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hindustan_Motors "Hindustan Motors"), [Premier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Premier_Automobiles_Limited "Premier Automobiles Limited"). Maruti Suzuki had a near [monopoly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monopoly "Monopoly") over the passenger cars segment. Tata and Mahindra were solely utility and commercial vehicle manufacturers, while Hindustan and Premier both built outdated and uncompetitive products.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_] [Daewoo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daewoo_Motors "Daewoo Motors") had entered the Indian automobile market with [Cielo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daewoo_Cielo "Daewoo Cielo") just three years back, while [Ford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ford_India_Private_Limited "Ford India Private Limited"), [Opel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Opel "Opel") and [Honda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Honda_Siel_Cars_India "Honda Siel Cars India") had entered less than a year back.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]
Hyundai Motor India Limited was formed on 6 May 1996 as a wholly owned subsidiary of [Hyundai Motor Company](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hyundai_Motor_Company "Hyundai Motor Company") of [South Korea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Korea "South Korea"). Its first manufacturing plant was constructed in [Irungattukottai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Irungattukottai "Irungattukottai") near [Chennai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chennai "Chennai"), [Tamil Nadu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tamil_Nadu "Tamil Nadu").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hyundai_Motor_India#cite_note-5) Its first car, the [Hyundai Santro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hyundai_Santro "Hyundai Santro"), was launched on 23 September 1998 and was a runaway success. Within a few months of its inception, HMIL became India's second-largest automobile manufacturer and the largest automobile exporter.
Mr Yang Soo Kim was then the managing director of Hyundai Motor India.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_] The Indian counterpart leadership team was managed by Mr AP Gandhi, Mr BVR Subbu and Mr G.S. Ramesh. Mr AP Gandhi was the president for a few years of inception. Mr BVR Subbu was the marketing director responsible for dealer development and sales. He resigned from Hyundai Motor India in 2006.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hyundai_Motor_India#cite_note-6)
HMC has set up a research and development facility (Hyundai Motor India Engineering – HMIE) in the cyber city of Hyderabad.
As HMC's global export hub for compact cars, HMIL became the first automotive company in India to achieve the export of 10 lakh cars in just over a decade. HMIL currently exports cars to more than 87 countries.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hyundai_Motor_India#cite_note-7)
In July 2012, [Arvind Saxena](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arvind_Saxena "Arvind Saxena"), the Director of Marketing and Sales stepped down from the position after serving the company for seven years.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hyundai_Motor_India#cite_note-8)
In August 2018, Rakesh Srivastava, Director of Sales and Marketing at Hyundai India, resigned from his position after serving for six years.
On 4 December 2018, Hyundai Motor India Ltd, announced the top-level management changes immediately. Seon Seob Kim assumed the responsibilities of MD and CEO from Young Key Koo.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]
In 2019, Hyundai Motor Company invested around 1.1 trillion KRW in an additional EV production line and began manufacturing Kona Electric.
In 2022, Hyundai Motor India Limited receives about 85% of its electrical power as eco-friendly energy from external power plants. Moreover, it is currently installing a stationary solar power system of 1.9MWp using the module factory's roof with a size of 13,028m².
On 15 June 2024, Hyundai Motor India filed a draft prospectus with the [Securities and Exchange Board of India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Securities_and_Exchange_Board_of_India "Securities and Exchange Board of India") seeking approval for an initial public offering.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hyundai_Motor_India#cite_note-9)
AS of 2025, HMIL is the second largest passenger car exporter and the second largest car manufacturer in India.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hyundai_Motor_India#cite_note-:0-10)
## Manufacturing facilities
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Hyundai_Motor_India&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Manufacturing facilities")]
HMIL has two manufacturing plants, one in [Irungattukottai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Irungattukottai "Irungattukottai"), [Tamil Nadu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tamil_Nadu "Tamil Nadu") and Other in [Talegaon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Talegaon "Talegaon"), [Maharashtra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maharashtra "Maharashtra"). [Irungattukottai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Irungattukottai "Irungattukottai") Plant has a capacity of 850,000 vehicles per annum.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hyundai_Motor_India#cite_note-11)
## R&D centre
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Hyundai_Motor_India&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: R&D centre")]
Hyundai Motor India Engineering (HMIE) is a fully owned subsidiary of Hyundai Motor Company, South Korea, which is located at Hyderabad, Telangana. HMIL established HMIE in November 2006 and contributed to the development of Hyundai Motors' popular new models for the Indian market starting with the Eon and followed now by the "i" series, and also in SUV segments like the Creta. Hyundai Motors' other overseas R&D centres are located in the United States, Germany, Japan, Korea, and China.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

Indian Quality Centre (INQC) is one of five quality centres worldwide, along with those in the US, China, Europe and Middle East.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hyundai_Motor_India#cite_note-12)
The India centre located at Faridabad, Haryana will conduct durability studies of existing models and benchmark parts and systems for constant improvement.
The key activity of the centre is to "contribute in new car development from pilot stage to create quality product with zero defect".
The centre will also be responsible for ensuring "top level safety quality" through proactive customer oriented management system and understanding feedback from them to eliminate potential risks. The centre also has an objective to study market conditions and other Asia Pacific regions to develop new cars and adapt strategies for continuous product quality improvement.
The company opened a training centre at the facility. It will have its own body and paint unit. The new service training will ensure overall skill development of entire service profile of dealer manpower.

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Hyundai_Motor_India&action=edit&section=13 "Edit section: Brand ambassador")]

## Hyundai Motor India Foundation
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Hyundai_Motor_India&action=edit&section=15 "Edit section: Hyundai Motor India Foundation")]
In 2021, the Hyundai Motor India Foundation (HMIF), the philanthropic arm of Hyundai Motor India Ltd., announced a new initiative, Art for Hope. It will work towards encouraging artists across various domains like digital arts, crafts, multidisciplinary arts, performance arts and visual arts. The project is scheduled to begin October 2021. Selected artists will get an opportunity to exchange ideas, complete an art project and be mentored by key industry people. The final projects will be displayed in art shows across India.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hyundai_Motor_India#cite_note-19)
## Potential Expansion
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Hyundai_Motor_India&action=edit&section=16 "Edit section: Potential Expansion")]
As of September 2026, there is conversation around expanding the footprint of Hyundai in India by adding a third plant by 2030 due to the expectation of India being an emerging growth market for Hyundai. The plan is in the early stages and a site has not been chosen, but the proposed plant would be large enough to increase production capacity within India by 500,000 units. This expansion would be in addition to the Sriperumbudur and Talegaon plants already within the country[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hyundai_Motor_India#cite_note-20).
